levelTitle: Level 0 - Basic Zero (Teen Startup) / Nivel 0 - Básico Cero

classes.classTitle: Class 1: Hello & Introductions / Saludos y Presentaciones
classes.classObjective: Presentarse con confianza y saludar en contextos formales e informales.
goals: Saludar de forma casual y formal (Hey!, Good morning, What's up?).
Presentarte diciendo tu nombre y cómo estás (I'm Alex, I'm great).
Preguntar el nombre a otros y despedirte con estilo (Nice to meet you, Bye!).

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The New Student / El Estudiante Nuevo 📱
sampleDialogue: Alex: 'Hey! What's up? Are you the new student at this school?'
Sam: 'Good morning! Yes, I am. My name is Sam. Nice to meet you!'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: First Impressions / Primeras Impresiones 🎧
listening.transcription: Good morning everyone! My name is Teacher David. I am very excited to meet all of you today. How is everyone feeling?
listening.audioTeacherText: Good morning everyone! My name is Teacher David. I am very excited to meet all of you today. How is everyone feeling?
listening.question: ¿Cómo saluda el profesor y cómo se siente hoy?
options: Dice Good morning y está muy emocionado de conocerlos a todos.
Dice Good night y está cansado por el viaje.
Dice Goodbye y se va al descanso.
listening.correctAnswerText: Dice Good morning y está muy emocionado de conocerlos a todos.

classes.classTitle: Class 2: Numbers, Age & Birthdays / Números, Edad y Cumpleaños
classes.classObjective: Expresar edad y fechas de cumpleaños usando 'I am' y preposiciones de tiempo.
goals: Decir tu edad usando 'I am [número] years old' (¡sin 'I have'!).
Nombrar los 12 meses del año en inglés.
Preguntar la edad y fecha de cumpleaños a tus amigos.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Mateo's Birthday Bash / El Cumpleaños de Mateo 🎂
sampleDialogue: Sofia: 'Happy birthday Mateo! You are finally 15 years old today!'
Mateo: 'Thank you Sofia! My birthday is always on October 12th and I feel awesome.'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Birthday Invitation / Invitación a la Fiesta 🎧
listening.transcription: Hey guys! I turn 16 this Saturday, October 12th. I am throwing a party at my house at 6:00 PM. Don't forget to come!
listening.audioTeacherText: Hey guys! I turn 16 this Saturday, October 12th. I am throwing a party at my house at 6:00 PM. Don't forget to come!
listening.question: ¿Cuántos años cumple y en qué fecha es la fiesta?
options: Cumple 16 años este sábado 12 de octubre.
Cumple 15 años el próximo año.
Cumple 18 años un domingo en la mañana.
listening.correctAnswerText: Cumple 16 años este sábado 12 de octubre.

classes.classTitle: Class 3: Family & Squad / Mi Familia y Amigos
classes.classObjective: Presentar a miembros de la familia y amigos usando 'my, his, her, our, their'.
goals: Nombrar miembros de la familia (parents, brother, sister, cousin).
Usar adjetivos posesivos con precisión (my, your, his, her, our, their).
Describir a tu mejor amigo/a y decir por qué es tu confidente.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Sofia's Medellín Squad / El Grupo de Sofía 🌇
sampleDialogue: Sofia: 'Carlos, look! This is a photo of my family. I live with my parents and my younger brother Daniel.'
Carlos: 'Awesome! And who is that girl with the skateboard? Is she your cousin?'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Meet the Family / Conoce a la Familia 🎧
listening.transcription: Hello class! I have a big family. I have two older brothers and one younger sister. We all live together in a cozy apartment with our cat.
listening.audioTeacherText: Hello class! I have a big family. I have two older brothers and one younger sister. We all live together in a cozy apartment with our cat.
listening.question: ¿Cómo está conformada la familia del profesor?
options: Tiene dos hermanos mayores, una hermana menor y un gato.
Es hijo único y no tiene mascotas.
Vive solo en una casa de campo.
listening.correctAnswerText: Tiene dos hermanos mayores, una hermana menor y un gato.

classes.classTitle: Class 4: Food, Drinks & Snacks / Comidas, Bebidas y Antojos
classes.classObjective: Expresar gustos y preferencias sobre comidas y bebidas usando 'like, love, don't like'.
goals: Nombrar comidas rápidas, frutas y bebidas populares.
Usar 'I like, I love, I prefer, I don't like' con fluidez.
Hacer pedidos y preguntar a tus amigos qué quieren comer.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Friday Food Fest / Viernes de Antojos 🍔
sampleDialogue: Camilo: 'Andrea, what do you want to order? I love pepperoni pizza and I always drink fresh juice.'
Andrea: 'I don't like spicy food or red meat. I prefer a fresh chicken wrap and cold lemonade.'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Ordering at the Counter / Pidiendo en el Mostrador 🎧
listening.transcription: Hi! Can I get one large pepperoni pizza, two orders of garlic bread, and a bottle of sparkling water, please?
listening.audioTeacherText: Hi! Can I get one large pepperoni pizza, two orders of garlic bread, and a bottle of sparkling water, please?
listening.question: ¿Qué está pidiendo el cliente?
options: Una pizza grande de pepperoni, dos panes de ajo y agua con gas.
Dos hamburguesas triples y una gaseosa de dieta.
Una ensalada de frutas y un café caliente.
listening.correctAnswerText: Una pizza grande de pepperoni, dos panes de ajo y agua con gas.

classes.classTitle: Class 5: Daily Routine & Time / Rutinas Diarias y Horarios
classes.classObjective: Describir rutinas diarias usando el presente simple y preposiciones de tiempo (at, in, on).
goals: Decir la hora en inglés (It's 6:30 AM, It's quarter past eight).
Usar verbos de rutina en Presente Simple (wake up, brush teeth, study, relax).
Manejar las preposiciones clave de tiempo: AT (la hora), IN (el momento), ON (días).

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: A Day in Santiago's Life / El Día de Santiago 📚
sampleDialogue: Santiago: 'Mariana, what time do you wake up on weekdays?'
Mariana: 'I wake up at 6:00 AM and have breakfast with my family in Bogotá.'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Morning Alarm / Alarma Matutina 🎧
listening.transcription: On weekdays, my alarm rings at 5:45 AM. I stretch, make my bed, and drink a hot cup of Colombian coffee before starting my classes.
listening.audioTeacherText: On weekdays, my alarm rings at 5:45 AM. I stretch, make my bed, and drink a hot cup of Colombian coffee before starting my classes.
listening.question: ¿A qué hora suena la alarma del profesor y qué hace primero?
options: Suena a las 5:45 AM, se estira, tiende su cama y toma café.
Suena a las 8:00 AM y sale corriendo sin desayunar.
No usa alarma porque se despierta al mediodía.
listening.correctAnswerText: Suena a las 5:45 AM, se estira, tiende su cama y toma café.

classes.classTitle: Class 6: Clothes & Streetwear / Ropa, Outfits y Estilo
classes.classObjective: Describir prendas de vestir y colores usando 'I wear, I am wearing, I like to wear'.
goals: Nombrar prendas populares (hoodie, jeans, sneakers, cap, t-shirt).
Describir lo que llevas puesto usando 'I wear' e 'I am wearing'.
Combinar adjetivos de color antes del sustantivo (a black jacket, white sneakers).

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Streetwear Shopping in Cali / De Compras en Cali 🛍️
sampleDialogue: Mateo: 'Lucas, what are you wearing to the party today?'
Lucas: 'I wear a black hoodie and white sneakers. It is stylish and comfortable.'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Describing a Party Look / El Look de la Fiesta 🎧
listening.transcription: Tonight I am wearing a black leather jacket, blue jeans, and clean white sneakers. It is stylish, simple, and very comfortable.
listening.audioTeacherText: Tonight I am wearing a black leather jacket, blue jeans, and clean white sneakers. It is stylish, simple, and very comfortable.
listening.question: ¿Qué prendas describe el profesor?
options: Chaqueta de cuero negra, jeans azules y tenis blancos limpios.
Un vestido formal rojo con zapatos de tacón.
Pijama deportiva para quedarse en casa.
listening.correctAnswerText: Chaqueta de cuero negra, jeans azules y tenis blancos limpios.

classes.classTitle: Class 7: Tech, Social Media & Hobbies / Redes, Apps y Tecnología
classes.classObjective: Expresar hábitos digitales y pasatiempos usando adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, sometimes, never).
goals: Nombrar plataformas, gadgets y pasatiempos digitales.
Usar adverbios de frecuencia: ALWAYS (100%), USUALLY (80%), SOMETIMES (50%), NEVER (0%).
Explicar qué tipo de contenido consumes o creas en internet.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Ultimate Gaming Weekend / Fin de Semana Gamer 🎮
sampleDialogue: Nicolas: 'Mariana, I always play online with my friends on Discord on Friday night.'
Mariana: 'Awesome! I sometimes post short videos on TikTok and watch gaming tutorials.'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Podcast & Playlist Habit / Hábitos Musicales 🎧
listening.transcription: I always listen to English podcasts while walking to class. It helps me improve my listening skills and discover new music from all over the world.
listening.audioTeacherText: I always listen to English podcasts while walking to class. It helps me improve my listening skills and discover new music from all over the world.
listening.question: ¿Qué hace el profesor mientras camina a clase?
options: Siempre escucha podcasts en inglés para mejorar su oído y descubrir música.
Juega videojuegos en su celular sin prestar atención.
Nunca usa audífonos porque no le gusta la música.
listening.correctAnswerText: Siempre escucha podcasts en inglés para mejorar su oído y descubrir música.

classes.classTitle: Class 8: Abilities & Sports / Talentos y Deportes (Can / Can't)
classes.classObjective: Expresar habilidades físicas y talentos usando 'can' y 'can't' con verbos de acción.
goals: Nombrar deportes y habilidades (swim, ride a bike, skateboard, draw, dance).
Usar el verbo modal CAN (puedo / sé hacer) y CAN'T (no puedo / no sé hacer).
Preguntar por talentos y habilidades a tus compañeros (Can you...?).

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The School Sports Festival / El Festival Deportivo 🏅
sampleDialogue: Daniel: 'Sofia, what sports or talents can you do for the festival?'
Sofia: 'I can ride a bike very fast and play soccer forward on the school team.'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Sports Tryouts / Pruebas de Equipo 🎧
listening.transcription: Welcome to soccer tryouts! If you can run, pass the ball accurately, and communicate well with your team, you have a great chance of making the squad.
listening.audioTeacherText: Welcome to soccer tryouts! If you can run, pass the ball accurately, and communicate well with your team, you have a great chance of making the squad.
listening.question: ¿Qué habilidades busca el entrenador para el equipo de fútbol?
options: Correr, pasar el balón con precisión y comunicarse bien en equipo.
Saber nadar y jugar videojuegos.
Llegar tarde y no pasar el balón.
listening.correctAnswerText: Correr, pasar el balón con precisión y comunicarse bien en equipo.

classes.classTitle: Class 9: My Hobbies & Free Time / Mis Pasatiempos y Tiempo Libre
classes.classObjective: Expresar gustos y pasatiempos juveniles usando verbos de preferencia (like, love, enjoy) con actividades en -ING y deportes con play, go y do.
goals: Expresar lo que amas hacer usando 'I like / I love / I enjoy + [Verbo-ING]'.
Usar los 3 verbos de acción para pasatiempos: PLAY (deportes con balón/juegos), GO (en -ing) y DO (individual/marcial).
Preguntar a tus amigos por sus hobbies con 'What do you like doing in your free time?'.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Weekend Squad Meetup / El Encuentro del Parche

sampleDialogue.speaker: Lucas
sampleDialogue.text: Hey Valeria! What do you like doing on Saturday afternoons?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Hola Valeria! ¿Qué te gusta hacer los sábados por la tarde?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valeria
sampleDialogue.text: I love skateboarding at the park with my friends and listening to upbeat music!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Amo patinar en el parque con mis amigos y escuchar música alegre!

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teen Podcast Host / El Podcaster Juvenil
listening.transcription: In my free time, I love playing the electric guitar and streaming video games with my squad on Discord.
listening.audioTeacherText: In my free time, I love playing the electric guitar and streaming video games with my squad on Discord.
listening.question: What does the speaker love doing in his free time?
options: Playing electric guitar and streaming video games with his squad.
Doing math homework all weekend long.
Sleeping 24 hours without eating.
listening.correctAnswerText: Playing electric guitar and streaming video games with his squad.

classes.classTitle: Class 10: Family & Friends / Mi Familia y Amigos
classes.classObjective: Presentar a miembros de la familia y amigos usando adjetivos posesivos (his, her, their, our) y describir personalidades básicas.
goals: Dominar los adjetivos posesivos: 'my', 'his' (de él), 'her' (de ella), 'our' (nuestro), 'their' (de ellos).
Nombrar miembros de la familia (parents, siblings, cousins) y describir su edad y profesión.
Formular preguntas sobre la familia ('Who is he/she?', 'How many siblings do you have?').

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Family Photo Album / El Álbum de Fotos

sampleDialogue.speaker: Santiago
sampleDialogue.text: Look at this photo! This is my older sister. Her name is Laura and her passion is digital photography.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Mira esta foto! Esta es mi hermana mayor. Su nombre es Laura y su pasión es la fotografía digital.

sampleDialogue.speaker: David
sampleDialogue.text: She looks very kind! And who is the boy with the skateboard next to your dad?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Se ve muy amable! ¿Y quién es el chico con la patineta al lado de tu papá?

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teen Describing Her Best Friend / Mi Mejor Amiga
listening.transcription: My best friend is Sofia. Her favorite hobby is playing the acoustic guitar and our dream is to form a musical band together.
listening.audioTeacherText: My best friend is Sofia. Her favorite hobby is playing the acoustic guitar and our dream is to form a musical band together.
listening.question: What is Sofia's favorite hobby and their shared dream?
options: Her hobby is playing acoustic guitar and their dream is forming a band.
Her hobby is sleeping all day and eating chips.
She does not like music at all.
listening.correctAnswerText: Her hobby is playing acoustic guitar and their dream is forming a band.

classes.classTitle: Class 11: Alphabet, Spelling & Social Usernames / Alfabeto, Deletreo y Usernames
classes.classObjective: Deletrear nombres propios, apellidos y dictar correos y usuarios de Instagram/Discord en inglés con pronunciación perfecta.
goals: Pronunciar las 26 letras del alfabeto inglés con ritmo y precisión fonética.
Deletrear tu nombre, apellido y ciudad natal con fluidez ('How do you spell that?').
Dictar correos electrónicos y tags de redes sociales usando símbolos digitales en inglés.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The International Esports Registration / El Registro de Esports

sampleDialogue.speaker: Official
sampleDialogue.text: Welcome to the tournament! What is your full name and how do you spell your gamer tag?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Bienvenido al torneo! ¿Cuál es tu nombre completo y cómo deletreas tu tag de jugador?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Camilo
sampleDialogue.text: My name is Camilo Vargas and my gamer tag is Vortex: V - O - R - T - E - X.
sampleDialogue.es: Mi nombre es Camilo Vargas y mi tag de jugador es Vortex: V - O - R - T - E - X.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Dictating a Gamer Email / Dictado de Correo
listening.transcription: My official email address is camilo_vargas at gmail dot com. That is C - A - M - I - L - O underscore V - A - R - G - A - S.
listening.audioTeacherText: My official email address is camilo_vargas at gmail dot com. That is C - A - M - I - L - O underscore V - A - R - G - A - S.
listening.question: What is the exact email address dictation?
options: camilo_vargas at gmail dot com
camilovargas123 at hotmail dot net
vortex_gamer at yahoo dot com
listening.correctAnswerText: camilo_vargas at gmail dot com

classes.classTitle: Class 12: Full Teen Profile: Age, Grade, City & Passions / Presentarse: Edad, Curso, Ciudad y Gustos
classes.classObjective: Realizar una presentación personal completa de 5 a 6 oraciones integrando To Be, edad, ciudad, gustos y pasatiempos en inglés.
goals: Presentarte con un pitch de 5 frases: nombre, edad, ciudad, grado escolar y gustos.
Usar 'I live in...', 'I study in grade...', 'In my free time I love...'.
Entrevistar a otros compañeros sobre su perfil completo con preguntas fluidas.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The International Youth Exchange Video / El Video de Intercambio

sampleDialogue.speaker: Mariana
sampleDialogue.text: Hello! My name is Mariana, I am fourteen years old and I live in Cali, Colombia.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Hola! Mi nombre es Mariana, tengo catorce años y vivo en Cali, Colombia.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Mariana
sampleDialogue.text: I study in ninth grade. In my free time, I love playing volleyball and listening to pop music.
sampleDialogue.es: Estudio en noveno grado. En mi tiempo libre, amo jugar voleibol y escuchar música pop.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Student Profile Pitch / Presentación de un Compañero
listening.transcription: Hello everyone! I am Carlos, I am fifteen years old, I live in Bogota and my biggest passion is programming video games.
listening.audioTeacherText: Hello everyone! I am Carlos, I am fifteen years old, I live in Bogota and my biggest passion is programming video games.
listening.question: Where does Carlos live and what is his biggest passion?
options: He lives in Bogota and his passion is programming video games.
He lives in Miami and hates computers.
He lives in London and only plays soccer.
listening.correctAnswerText: He lives in Bogota and his passion is programming video games.

classes.classTitle: Class 13: Clothes, Personal Style & Streetwear / Ropa, Estilo Personal y Apariencia
classes.classObjective: Describir atuendos y estilo personal usando 'wear / wearing', colores, prendas juveniles y prendas singulares vs plurales en inglés.
goals: Usar 'I am wearing...' para describir tu ropa actual (hoodie, t-shirt, jeans, sneakers).
Diferenciar prendas singulares ('a jacket') de prendas siempre plurales ('jeans', 'glasses', 'sneakers').
Preguntar a otros qué llevan puesto ('What are you wearing today?').

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Streetwear Shopping Spree / De Compras en el Centro Comercial

sampleDialogue.speaker: Tomás
sampleDialogue.text: Look at this purple oversized hoodie Sara! Do you think it matches my black cargo pants?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Mira este buzo morado holgado Sara! ¿Crees que combina con mis pantalones cargo negros?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Sara
sampleDialogue.text: Yes, it looks amazing! I am wearing a denim jacket and white sneakers to the festival.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Sí, se ve increíble! Yo voy a llevar puesta una chaqueta de jean y tenis blancos al festival.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Describing a Lost Backpack / Descripción de Ropa
listening.transcription: Today I am wearing a comfortable grey hoodie, dark blue jeans, and my favorite white athletic sneakers.
listening.audioTeacherText: Today I am wearing a comfortable grey hoodie, dark blue jeans, and my favorite white athletic sneakers.
listening.question: What outfit is the speaker wearing today?
options: A grey hoodie, dark blue jeans, and white athletic sneakers.
A formal suit and yellow plastic boots.
A swimming suit and winter gloves.
listening.correctAnswerText: A grey hoodie, dark blue jeans, and white athletic sneakers.

classes.classTitle: Class 14: School Subjects & Classroom Life / Escuela, Materias y Objetos del Salón
classes.classObjective: Nombrar materias del colegio, describir objetos escolares usando demostrativos (this/that/these/those) y expresar materias favoritas.
goals: Nombrar materias escolares: Math, Science, History, English, Arts, Physical Education (PE).
Dominar los 4 demostrativos: THIS (cerca singular), THAT (lejos singular), THESE (cerca plural), THOSE (lejos plural).
Expresar tus materias favoritas con 'My favorite school subject is...' y dar razones.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The First Day at High School / El Primer Día de Colegio

sampleDialogue.speaker: Daniel
sampleDialogue.text: Look Laura! This is our new English classroom and that is the modern computer lab!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Mira Laura! ¡Este es nuestro nuevo salón de inglés y ese es el laboratorio moderno de computadores!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Laura
sampleDialogue.text: It looks awesome! And these are my colorful notebooks for Math and Science class.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Se ve genial! Y estos son mis cuadernos coloridos para la clase de Matemáticas y Ciencias.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teacher Explaining School Schedule / El Horario Escolar
listening.transcription: Good morning class! Today we have Math first, and right after the morning break, we have our fun Science experiment in the chemistry lab.
listening.audioTeacherText: Good morning class! Today we have Math first, and right after the morning break, we have our fun Science experiment in the chemistry lab.
listening.question: What class do students have right after the morning break?
options: Science experiment in the chemistry lab.
Sleeping class in the dormitory.
Video game tournament in the cafeteria.
listening.correctAnswerText: Science experiment in the chemistry lab.

classes.classTitle: Class 15: Basic Daily Routine & Clock Time / Rutina Diaria y Horarios
classes.classObjective: Describir tu día típico de principio a fin usando verbos de rutina diaria en Presente Simple y conectores de tiempo (at, in the morning/afternoon).
goals: Narrar tu rutina matutina, escolar y nocturna en Presente Simple.
Usar la preposición de hora 'at' (at 6:00 AM, at 2:30 PM) y momentos del día ('in the morning', 'at night').
Preguntar la hora y los hábitos diarios con 'What time do you wake up?'.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: A Day in the Life of a Teen Athlete / Un Día en la Vida de un Atleta

sampleDialogue.speaker: Felipe
sampleDialogue.text: Every morning, I wake up at 5:45 AM, have a protein breakfast, and go to soccer training at 6:30 AM.
sampleDialogue.es: Todas las mañanas, me despierto a las 5:45 AM, tomo un desayuno con proteína y voy a entrenamiento de fútbol a las 6:30 AM.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valeria
sampleDialogue.text: That is super early! And what time do you arrive at school for your academic classes?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Eso es súper temprano! ¿Y a qué hora llegas al colegio para tus clases académicas?

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teen Vlogger's Daily Schedule / La Rutina de la Vlogger
listening.transcription: On school days, I wake up at 6:30 AM, attend classes until 2:30 PM, and have dinner with my family at 7:30 PM.
listening.audioTeacherText: On school days, I wake up at 6:30 AM, attend classes until 2:30 PM, and have dinner with my family at 7:30 PM.
listening.question: What time does the speaker wake up and have dinner on school days?
options: Wakes up at 6:30 AM and has dinner at 7:30 PM.
Wakes up at 12:00 PM and never eats dinner.
Wakes up at 3:00 AM and sleeps during class.
listening.correctAnswerText: Wakes up at 6:30 AM and has dinner at 7:30 PM.

classes.classTitle: Class 16: Level 0 Grand Review & Final Challenge 🏆 / Repaso General y Graduación
classes.classObjective: Integrar los 15 temas de Nivel 0 (To Be, posesivos, gustos con -ing, demostrativos, deletreo y rutina diaria) en un video proyecto de graduación.
goals: Integrar tu biografía completa (To Be, edad, ciudad, familia, gustos con -ING y rutina).
Deletrear tu nombre y responder preguntas de conversación con total naturalidad.
Grabar tu presentación oficial de graduación de Nivel 0 con entusiasmo y seguridad.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Level 0 Graduation Speech / El Discurso de Graduación

sampleDialogue.speaker: Santiago
sampleDialogue.text: Hello everyone! Today we are proud Level 0 graduates! We know how to introduce ourselves, describe our families, and speak about our daily routines in English.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Hola a todos! ¡Hoy somos orgullosos graduados de Nivel 0! Sabemos cómo presentarnos, describir a nuestras familias y hablar de nuestras rutinas diarias en inglés.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: We also master our favorite hobbies with -ING, describe our streetwear outfits, and spell any word with the English alphabet.
sampleDialogue.es: También dominamos nuestros pasatiempos con -ING, describimos nuestros outfits de ropa y deletreamos cualquier palabra con el alfabeto inglés.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Director's Graduation Toast / El Brindis de Graduación
listening.transcription: Congratulations teens! You have completed all 16 classes of Level 0 with total dedication, and you now speak English with great confidence and clear pronunciation.
listening.audioTeacherText: Congratulations teens! You have completed all 16 classes of Level 0 with total dedication, and you now speak English with great confidence and clear pronunciation.
listening.question: What did the students achieve in Level 0 according to the director?
options: Completed all 16 classes and speak English with confidence and clear pronunciation.
Failed all classes and need to start over.
Decided to never study English again.
listening.correctAnswerText: Completed all 16 classes and speak English with confidence and clear pronunciation.

levelTitle: Level 1 - Basic 1 (Teen Explorer Studio) / Nivel 1 - Básico 1 (Adolescente Explorador)

classes.classTitle: Class 1: People in Your Circle & Personality / Personas de tu Círculo y Personalidad
classes.classObjective: Describir amigos de tu círculo social con rasgos de personalidad y usar HAVE vs HAS correctamente.
goals: Identificar y usar 6 adjetivos clave para describir personalidades juveniles.
Aplicar la regla de HAVE (I/You/We/They) vs. HAS (He/She) para rasgos y pertenencias.
Crear el perfil completo de un amigo combinando personalidad, rasgos y estados de ánimo.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Medellín Science Squad / El Equipo de Ciencias 🧪
sampleDialogue: Emma: 'Lucas, look at our project group! I have three awesome classmates on our team.'
Lucas: 'Awesome! What is Leo like? Is he quiet or outgoing?'

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Meet My Teammate / Conoce a mi Compañero 🎧
listening.transcription: Welcome to our team! My best friend Leo is super creative and always has cool ideas for our school projects. He is very friendly, loyal, and loves meeting new people.
listening.audioTeacherText: Welcome to our team! My best friend Leo is super creative and always has cool ideas for our school projects. He is very friendly, loyal, and loves meeting new people.

Ubicar correctamente adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, sometimes, rarely, never).
Explicar beneficios con 'I practice [Sport] [Frequency] because it helps me [Benefit]'.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Ultimate Teen Fitness Routine ⚽🚴‍♀️

sampleDialogue.speaker: Felipe
sampleDialogue.text: Laura, you look full of energy today! How often do you practice sports during the week?
sampleDialogue.es: Laura, ¡te ves llena de energía hoy! ¿Con qué frecuencia practicas deportes durante la semana?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Laura
sampleDialogue.text: I usually go cycling four times a week along the mountain trail, and I always drink lots of water.
sampleDialogue.es: Normalmente salgo a montar en bicicleta cuatro veces por semana por la trocha de montaña, y siempre tomo mucha agua.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Coach Martinez's Golden Health Tips 🎧
listening.transcription: Maintaining a healthy lifestyle as a teenager is easier than you think. First, always drink at least two liters of fresh water daily, especially before and after workouts. Second, athletes should sleep eight hours every night because deep rest recovers your muscles and boosts memory. Finally, try to play a sport or walk outside at least three times a week.
listening.audioTeacherText: Maintaining a healthy lifestyle as a teenager is easier than you think. First, always drink at least two liters of fresh water daily, especially before and after workouts. Second, athletes should sleep eight hours every night because deep rest recovers your muscles and boosts memory. Finally, try to play a sport or walk outside at least three times a week.
listening.question: Why should athletes sleep eight hours every night according to the coach?
options: Because deep rest recovers muscles and boosts memory.
Because they don't want to go to school.
Because sleeping makes them run ten times faster.
listening.correctAnswerText: Because deep rest recovers muscles and boosts memory.

classes.classTitle: Class 8: City Outings, Hangouts & Weekend Plans / Salidas y Planes de Fin de Semana
classes.classObjective: Proponer salidas con amigos usando Let's + base verb, How about + -ing, horas y lugares de encuentro.
goals: Nombrar lugares de entretenimiento urbano (cinema, skatepark, arcade, bowling, food trucks).
Proponer planes con LET'S [Base verb] y HOW ABOUT [Verb-ING]?
Coordinar horarios y puntos de encuentro con 'Let's meet at [Time] in front of [Place]'.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Weekend Squad Chat 📱🎟️

sampleDialogue.speaker: Andrés
sampleDialogue.text: Hey squad! Are you free this Saturday afternoon? Let's go to the shopping mall and hang out!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Hola grupo! ¿Están libres este sábado en la tarde? ¡Vamos al centro comercial a parchar!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valeria
sampleDialogue.text: Count me in! How about watching the new superhero premiere at 4:00 PM at the cinema?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Cuenta conmigo! ¿Qué tal si vemos el estreno de superhéroes a las 4:00 PM en el cine?

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Confirming the Saturday Squad Plan 🎧
listening.transcription: Hey guys! I just booked our tickets for the escape room challenge this Saturday. Let's meet at 2:45 PM in front of the fountain at Central Mall. Afterward, how about grabbing bubble tea and hanging out at the skatepark? Make sure to bring your transit card and be on time!
listening.audioTeacherText: Hey guys! I just booked our tickets for the escape room challenge this Saturday. Let's meet at 2:45 PM in front of the fountain at Central Mall. Afterward, how about grabbing bubble tea and hanging out at the skatepark? Make sure to bring your transit card and be on time!
listening.question: Where and what time are they meeting on Saturday?
options: At 6:00 PM inside the dark parking lot.
At 2:45 PM in front of the fountain at Central Mall.
On Monday morning at school.
listening.correctAnswerText: At 2:45 PM in front of the fountain at Central Mall.

classes.classTitle: Class 9: Entertainment Reviews: Series, Movies & Games / Reseñas de Medios y Entretenimiento
classes.classObjective: Expresar opiniones críticas sobre series, películas, juegos y música usando adjetivos descriptivos (masterpiece, addictive, overrated) y conectores.
goals: Usar adjetivos de opinión avanzados (masterpiece, addictive, overrated, thrilling, captivating).
Estructurar reseñas con 'In my opinion, [Title] is [Adjective] because [Reason]'.
Contrastar pros y contras usando el conector ALTHOUGH / BUT.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Ultimate Game & Anime Debate 🎮🎬

sampleDialogue.speaker: Camila
sampleDialogue.text: Esteban, did you finish watching the new anime series Arcane? What was your final review?
sampleDialogue.es: Esteban, ¿terminaste de ver la serie de anime Arcane? ¿Cuál fue tu reseña final?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Esteban
sampleDialogue.text: In my opinion, it is an absolute masterpiece! The animation is breathtaking and the characters feel real.
sampleDialogue.es: En mi opinión, ¡es una obra maestra absoluta! La animación es impresionante y los personajes se sienten reales.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Pop Culture Podcast Segment 🎧
listening.transcription: Welcome back to Teen Media Radar! Today we are reviewing the latest sci-fi movie. In my opinion, the film is action-packed and highly entertaining from start to finish. Although some plot twists are a bit predictable, the outstanding soundtrack and CGI visual effects make it a must-watch experience on the big screen.
listening.audioTeacherText: Welcome back to Teen Media Radar! Today we are reviewing the latest sci-fi movie. In my opinion, the film is action-packed and highly entertaining from start to finish. Although some plot twists are a bit predictable, the outstanding soundtrack and CGI visual effects make it a must-watch experience on the big screen.
listening.question: Why is the movie a must-watch experience according to the podcast host?
options: Because it is very short and boring.
Because of its outstanding soundtrack and CGI visual effects.
Because it has no sound or special effects.
listening.correctAnswerText: Because of its outstanding soundtrack and CGI visual effects.

classes.classTitle: Class 10: Level 2 Capstone: Teen Podcast & Grand Review / Gran Graduación y Repaso de Retos
classes.classObjective: Integrar y demostrar fluidez oral en todas las estructuras del Nivel 2 a través de debates y el podcast de graduación.
goals: Conectar con fluidez todas las estructuras del Nivel 2 (Can, There is/are, Go by, Must/Should, Reviews).
Participar en debates juveniles respondiendo con argumentos y conectores (because, but, although).
Grabar el discurso de graduación del Nivel 2 demostrando pronunciación clara y confianza.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Level 2 Graduation Podcast Live! 🎙️🌟

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: Welcome to the season finale of Teen Voices Live! Mateo, can you believe we just completed Level 2?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Bienvenidos al episodio final de temporada de Teen Voices Live! Mateo, ¿puedes creer que acabamos de completar el Nivel 2?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Mateo
sampleDialogue.text: It feels incredible! We started describing simple animals and now we can debate future careers, rules, and urban plans.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Se siente increíble! Empezamos describiendo animales sencillos y ahora podemos debatir sobre carreras, normas y planes urbanos.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Level 2 Master Graduation Message 🎧
listening.transcription: Congratulations on completing all ten classes of Teens Basic 2 Communicator! You have mastered discussing animal habitats, home layout, urban transit, future careers, abilities, rules, sports routines, weekend plans, and media reviews. You are now fully prepared to enter Level 3 and take your English debates, storytelling, and global communication to the next level!
listening.audioTeacherText: Congratulations on completing all ten classes of Teens Basic 2 Communicator! You have mastered discussing animal habitats, home layout, urban transit, future careers, abilities, rules, sports routines, weekend plans, and media reviews. You are now fully prepared to enter Level 3 and take your English debates, storytelling, and global communication to the next level!
listening.question: What does the teacher confirm you are ready for at the end of the message?
options: To enter Level 3 and take debates and storytelling to the next level.
To stop learning and forget all English vocabulary.
To only watch silent movies.
listening.correctAnswerText: To enter Level 3 and take debates and storytelling to the next level.

classes.classTitle: Class 1: Daily Routine & Time / Rutina Diaria y la Hora
classes.classObjective: Comunicar tu horario semanal, hábitos de estudio y momentos clave del día en inglés.
goals: Decir la hora en formato digital y tradicional (half past, quarter to, at 6:30 AM).
Describir tu rutina diaria usando Present Simple con conectores temporales.
Utilizar adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, sometimes, never) en el orden correcto.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Lucas's Busy Weekday / El Día Ocupado de Lucas

sampleDialogue.speaker: Lucas
sampleDialogue.text: Hey Valentina! What time do you usually leave for school in the morning?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Hola Valentina! ¿A qué hora sales normalmente para el colegio por la mañana?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: I always leave at quarter past seven because my bus arrives at seven thirty.
sampleDialogue.es: Siempre salgo a las siete y cuarto porque mi bus llega a las siete y media.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Coach Ramirez's Schedule / El Horario del Entrenador
listening.transcription: Our soccer training always starts at half past four in the afternoon. Please do not be late because we have a big match on Friday.
listening.audioTeacherText: Our soccer training always starts at half past four in the afternoon. Please do not be late because we have a big match on Friday.
listening.question: What time does the soccer training start?
options: At half past four in the afternoon (4:30 PM).
At quarter to four in the morning (3:45 AM).
At five o'clock in the evening (5:00 PM).
listening.correctAnswerText: At half past four in the afternoon (4:30 PM).

classes.classTitle: Class 2: Sports, Competitions & Teams / Deportes, Competencias y Equipos
classes.classObjective: Hablar de tus deportes favoritos, torneos colegiales y hábitos deportivos usando Play, Do y Go.
goals: Diferenciar y usar correctamente Play (balón/equipo), Go (-ing) y Do (artes marciales/individual).
Describir resultados deportivos, posiciones en la cancha y momentos de partido.
Preguntar y responder sobre entrenamientos, torneos y atletas favoritos.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Final Match! / ¡El Partido Final!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Camilo
sampleDialogue.text: Are you ready for the final match this Friday against San Jose school?
sampleDialogue.es: ¿Estás lista para el partido final este viernes contra el colegio San José?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Sofía
sampleDialogue.text: Yes! We train every day, and our goalkeeper is playing better than ever.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Sí! Entrenamos todos los días y nuestra portera está jugando mejor que nunca.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Captain's Pre-Match Speech / El Discurso del Capitán
listening.transcription: Listen up team! We need to pass the ball quickly, stay strong on defense, and support our striker. We can win this trophy together!
listening.audioTeacherText: Listen up team! We need to pass the ball quickly, stay strong on defense, and support our striker. We can win this trophy together!
listening.question: What is the captain's main instruction to the team?
options: To pass the ball quickly and stay strong on defense.
To leave the pitch and play video games instead.
To let the rival team score five goals.
listening.correctAnswerText: To pass the ball quickly and stay strong on defense.

classes.classTitle: Class 3: Holidays, Festivals & Traditions / Días Festivos, Festivales y Tradiciones
classes.classObjective: Describir celebraciones culturales, fiestas familiares y festividades globales usando preposiciones de tiempo con precisión.
goals: Dominar el uso de preposiciones temporales: In (meses/años), On (días/fechas), At (horas/fiestas puntuales).
Describir costumbres familiares, disfraces, platos típicos y decoraciones.
Preguntar y responder sobre planes festivos y recuerdos de celebraciones pasadas.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Little Candles Night! / ¡La Noche de las Velitas!

sampleDialogue.speaker: John
sampleDialogue.text: Mariana, what is that beautiful tradition you celebrate on December 7th?
sampleDialogue.es: Mariana, ¿cuál es esa hermosa tradición que celebran el 7 de diciembre?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Mariana
sampleDialogue.text: It is Little Candles' Day! In the evening, we light colorful candles outside our homes.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Es el Día de las Velitas! Por la tarde-noche, encendemos velas coloridas afuera de nuestras casas.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: New Year Traditions / Tradiciones de Año Nuevo
listening.transcription: Every year on December 31st at midnight, we eat twelve grapes and run around the block with suitcases for good travel luck!
listening.audioTeacherText: Every year on December 31st at midnight, we eat twelve grapes and run around the block with suitcases for good travel luck!
listening.question: When does this traditional New Year celebration happen?
options: On December 31st at midnight (12:00 AM).
In July on a sunny Friday afternoon.
On October 31st during Halloween night.
listening.correctAnswerText: On December 31st at midnight (12:00 AM).

classes.classTitle: Class 4: Space, Science & Future / El Espacio, la Ciencia y el Futuro
classes.classObjective: Hacer predicciones sobre el futuro de la tecnología, inteligencia artificial y el cosmos usando Will y Won't.
goals: Usar 'Will' (+) y 'Won't' (-) para expresar predicciones sobre el futuro.
Describir avances de inteligencia artificial, exploración planetaria y tecnología espacial.
Formular preguntas futuristas ('Will robots replace teachers?') y responder con argumentos.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Mission to Mars 2040 / Misión a Marte 2040

sampleDialogue.speaker: Astrid
sampleDialogue.text: Do you think our generation will travel to Mars before 2045?
sampleDialogue.es: ¿Crees que nuestra generación viajará a Marte antes del 2045?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Diego
sampleDialogue.text: Absolutely! Nuclear rockets will reach Mars in only four weeks instead of seven months.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Totalmente! Los cohetes nucleares llegarán a Marte en solo cuatro semanas en vez de siete meses.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: AI Professor's Forecast / El Pronóstico de la IA
listening.transcription: In the next thirty years, artificial intelligence will help humans discover clean fusion energy, but it will not replace human creativity or empathy.
listening.audioTeacherText: In the next thirty years, artificial intelligence will help humans discover clean fusion energy, but it will not replace human creativity or empathy.
listening.question: What does the professor predict about artificial intelligence?
options: It will help discover clean fusion energy, but won't replace human creativity.
It will destroy all computers and telescopes on Earth.
It will stop space exploration completely in two years.
listening.correctAnswerText: It will help discover clean fusion energy, but won't replace human creativity.

classes.classTitle: Class 5: Past To Be: Was/Were & Childhood Memories / Pasado To Be y Recuerdos de Infancia
classes.classObjective: Contar recuerdos del pasado, describir cómo eras de niño y ubicar eventos históricos usando Was y Were.
goals: Dominar la diferencia entre Was (I/He/She/It) y Were (You/We/They) en afirmativo y negativo (Wasn't / Weren't).
Describir tu personalidad, juguetes favoritos y emociones en la escuela primaria.
Preguntar sobre lugares del pasado ('Where were you yesterday?') y responder con confianza.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Old Photo Album / El Álbum de Fotos Viejas

sampleDialogue.speaker: Paula
sampleDialogue.text: Look at this photo Andrés! You were so small and your hair was curly!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Mira esta foto Andrés! ¡Eras tan pequeño y tu cabello era rizado!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Andrés
sampleDialogue.text: Haha yes! I was six years old in that picture and we were at Disney park.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Jaja sí! Yo tenía seis años en esa foto y estábamos en el parque de Disney.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teacher's First Day Memory / El Primer Día del Profe
listening.transcription: On my first day of primary school, I was very nervous because the school was huge, but my teacher was super friendly and welcoming.
listening.audioTeacherText: On my first day of primary school, I was very nervous because the school was huge, but my teacher was super friendly and welcoming.
listening.question: How was the teacher feeling on the first day of primary school?
options: Very nervous because the school was huge.
Angry and fighting with other classmates.
Asleep in the car until noon.
listening.correctAnswerText: Very nervous because the school was huge.

classes.classTitle: Class 6: Vacations, Travel & Anecdotes / Vacaciones, Viajes y Anécdotas
classes.classObjective: Narrar viajes de vacaciones, experiencias turísticas y anécdotas divertidas usando verbos regulares en pasado.
goals: Formar y pronunciar oraciones en Pasado Simple con verbos regulares (-ed).
Describir actividades turísticas: visitar museos, caminar por playas y probar comida local.
Usar 'Did you...?' para preguntar sobre viajes pasados y responder con fluidez.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The San Andrés Adventure / La Aventura en San Andrés

sampleDialogue.speaker: Sebastián
sampleDialogue.text: Laura! Did you travel anywhere exciting during the mid-year break?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Laura! ¿Viajaste a algún lugar emocionante durante el descanso de mitad de año?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Laura
sampleDialogue.text: Yes! We visited San Andres Island. We rented a golf cart and explored the whole island.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Sí! Visitamos la Isla de San Andrés. Alquilamos un carrito de golf y exploramos toda la isla.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Camping Anecdote / La Anécdota del Camping
listening.transcription: Last summer we camped near the lake. At midnight it started to rain heavily, so we packed our sleeping bags and slept inside the car!
listening.audioTeacherText: Last summer we camped near the lake. At midnight it started to rain heavily, so we packed our sleeping bags and slept inside the car!
listening.question: Why did they sleep inside the car during the camping trip?
options: Because it started to rain heavily at midnight.
Because they lost their car keys in the lake.
Because a bear entered their hotel room.
listening.correctAnswerText: Because it started to rain heavily at midnight.

classes.classTitle: Class 7: Biographies of Artists, Athletes & Creators / Biografías de Creadores y Atletas
classes.classObjective: Narrar biografías de celebridades, deportistas y científicos usando verbos irregulares en Pasado Simple.
goals: Dominar los verbos irregulares más frecuentes para biografías (went, won, wrote, gave, had).
Estructurar líneas de tiempo biográficas: nacimiento, juventud, lucha y mayor logro.
Preguntar y responder sobre los momentos cumbre de figuras mundiales y colombianas.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Inspiring Rise of Lucho Díaz / El Ascenso de Lucho

sampleDialogue.speaker: Narrator
sampleDialogue.text: Luis Diaz was born in Barrancas, a small indigenous town in La Guajira.
sampleDialogue.es: Luis Díaz nació en Barrancas, un pequeño pueblo indígena en La Guajira.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Narrator
sampleDialogue.text: He grew up playing barefoot on dusty fields, but he never gave up on his dream.
sampleDialogue.es: Creció jugando descalzo en canchas polvorientas, pero nunca se rindió en su sueño.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Shakira's Early Breakthrough / El Salto de Shakira
listening.transcription: Shakira wrote her first poem at age four and composed her first song at age eight. Later, she moved to the United States and became a global music icon.
listening.audioTeacherText: Shakira wrote her first poem at age four and composed her first song at age eight. Later, she moved to the United States and became a global music icon.
listening.question: At what age did Shakira write her first poem?
options: At age four (4 years old).
At age twenty after university.
At age fifteen during high school.
listening.correctAnswerText: At age four (4 years old).

classes.classTitle: Class 8: Storytelling Connectors / Conectores para Contar Historias
classes.classObjective: Estructurar y narrar anécdotas, historias de misterio y sucesos inesperados usando conectores de secuencia y contraste.
goals: Usar conectores de inicio, giro inesperado y desenlace (First, Suddenly, Fortunately, In the end).
Construir historias con introducción, nudo emocionante y resolución clara.
Relatar una anécdota personal divertida o misteriosa manteniendo al oyente enganchado.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Creepy Sound in the Attic / El Ruido en el Ático

sampleDialogue.speaker: Felipe
sampleDialogue.text: First, the storm started and the power went out completely.
sampleDialogue.es: Primero, comenzó la tormenta y se fue la luz por completo.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Sara
sampleDialogue.text: Suddenly, we heard heavy scratching footsteps above our heads in the attic!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡De repente, escuchamos pasos y rasguños pesados arriba de nuestras cabezas en el ático!

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: The Lost Backpack Anecdote / La Mochila Perdida
listening.transcription: I thought I lost my backpack at the mall. Suddenly, my brother called me on my phone. Fortunately, he had my backpack in his car the whole time!
listening.audioTeacherText: I thought I lost my backpack at the mall. Suddenly, my brother called me on my phone. Fortunately, he had my backpack in his car the whole time!
listening.question: How was the mystery of the lost backpack resolved?
options: Fortunately, his brother had the backpack in his car the whole time.
He bought a new backpack in a foreign country.
A thief ran away with all his school notebooks.
listening.correctAnswerText: Fortunately, his brother had the backpack in his car the whole time.

classes.classTitle: Class 9: Everyday Problems & How to Explain Them / Problemas Cotidianos y Soluciones
classes.classObjective: Explicar problemas de la vida diaria, fallas de dispositivos y solicitar ayuda o favores en inglés con educación.
goals: Describir problemas cotidianos: 'My battery died', 'The wifi is down', 'I forgot my keys'.
Hacer peticiones formales y corteses usando 'Could you please...?' y 'Can I borrow...?'.
Proponer soluciones prácticas para ayudar a amigos en apuros.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: Low Battery Emergency! / ¡Emergencia de Batería Baja!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Kevin
sampleDialogue.text: Juliana, I have a big problem! My phone battery died and my mom is waiting outside.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Juliana, tengo un gran problema! La batería de mi celular murió y mi mamá está esperando afuera.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Juliana
sampleDialogue.text: Don't panic! Could you use my phone to call her right now?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡No entres en pánico! ¿Podrías usar mi celular para llamarla ahora mismo?

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Broken Laptop Problem / El Portátil Bloqueado
listening.transcription: Excuse me teacher, my laptop screen froze completely during the presentation. Could you please give me two minutes to restart it?
listening.audioTeacherText: Excuse me teacher, my laptop screen froze completely during the presentation. Could you please give me two minutes to restart it?
listening.question: What polite request does the student make to the teacher?
options: Could you please give me two minutes to restart my laptop?
Could you buy me a brand new computer right now?
Could you cancel the class for the whole semester?
listening.correctAnswerText: Could you please give me two minutes to restart my laptop?

classes.classTitle: Class 10: Irregular Verbs & -ed Endings (Video Project) / Verbos Irregulares y Proyecto Final
classes.classObjective: Pronunciar con precisión nativa las terminaciones -ed, dominar el catálogo de verbos irregulares y presentar el proyecto final de video en inglés.
goals: Distinguir y pronunciar con precisión los 3 sonidos de -ed: /t/ (walked), /d/ (played) y /ɪd/ (visited/needed).
Dominar los 20 verbos irregulares indispensables de nivel básico con cero vacilaciones.
Grabar o presentar tu discurso de graduación en video narrando un logro del cual estés orgulloso.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Level 3 Graduation Speech / Discurso de Graduación

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: When I started Level 3, I was nervous and didn't speak with confidence.
sampleDialogue.es: Cuando comencé el Nivel 3, estaba nerviosa y no hablaba con confianza.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: Then, I practiced every day, learned irregular verbs, and explored exciting topics.
sampleDialogue.es: Luego, practiqué todos los días, aprendí verbos irregulares y exploré temas emocionantes.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Pronunciation Test / Test de Pronunciación de -ED
listening.transcription: Yesterday I walked to school (/t/), played soccer with my friends (/d/), and visited my grandparents (/ɪd/).
listening.audioTeacherText: Yesterday I walked to school (/t/), played soccer with my friends (/d/), and visited my grandparents (/ɪd/).
listening.question: Which of the three verbs in the teacher's audio is pronounced with the /ɪd/ sound?
options: Visited (/vɪzɪtɪd/) because the base verb ends in the letter T.
Walked because it sounds like Spanish.
Played because it ends in letter Y.
listening.correctAnswerText: Visited (/vɪzɪtɪd/) because the base verb ends in the letter T.

levelTitle: Level 4: Teen Leader & Debates (B1 Threshold) / Nivel 4: Liderazgo y Debate

classes.classTitle: Class 1: My Opinions & Perspectives / Mis Opiniones y Perspectivas
classes.classObjective: Expresar opiniones fundamentadas, acuerdos y desacuerdos corteses sobre música, tecnología y tendencias usando conectores de justificación.
goals: Dominar frases de opinión: 'In my opinion', 'I strongly believe', 'From my perspective'.
Expresar acuerdo ('I totally agree with you') y desacuerdo cortés ('I see your point, but...').
Justificar tus ideas usando 'because', 'since' y ejemplos reales de la vida juvenil.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The High School Debate / El Debate Estudiantil

sampleDialogue.speaker: Camilo
sampleDialogue.text: In my opinion, smartphones should be permitted in classrooms for research and educational apps.
sampleDialogue.es: En mi opinión, los celulares deberían permitirse en los salones para investigación y apps educativas.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Natalia
sampleDialogue.text: I see your point, but many students get distracted playing games and checking notifications.
sampleDialogue.es: Entiendo tu punto, pero muchos estudiantes se distraen jugando y revisando notificaciones.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teacher's Perspective on Exams / La Postura del Profesor
listening.transcription: From my perspective, practical oral presentations and team projects demonstrate real English fluency much better than traditional multiple-choice grammar exams.
listening.audioTeacherText: From my perspective, practical oral presentations and team projects demonstrate real English fluency much better than traditional multiple-choice grammar exams.
listening.question: What is the teacher's perspective on student evaluation?
options: Practical presentations demonstrate real fluency better than traditional exams.
Students should only do written grammar tests every single day.
Oral English practice is completely unnecessary.
listening.correctAnswerText: Practical presentations demonstrate real fluency better than traditional exams.

classes.classTitle: Class 2: Giving Good Advice / Dar Buenos Consejos
classes.classObjective: Dar y pedir consejos empáticos ante dilemas de estudio, amistades y hábitos usando Should, Shouldn't y Why don't you.
goals: Usar 'You should' (+) y 'You shouldn't' (-) seguidos de verbo base para dar recomendaciones.
Proponer sugerencias dinámicas con 'Why don't you...?' y 'If I were you, I would...'.
Pedir orientación ('What should I do?') y responder con empatía y tacto.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Stressed Student Dilemma / El Estudiante Estresado

sampleDialogue.speaker: Lucas
sampleDialogue.text: Sofía, I have three huge tests this Friday and I feel super overwhelmed! What should I do?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Sofía
sampleDialogue.text: Don't panic Lucas! First, you should make a clear priority list and study one subject at a time.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡No entres en pánico Lucas! Primero, deberías hacer una lista clara de prioridades y estudiar una materia a la vez.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Doctor's Advice on Sleep / El Consejo del Médico

listening.audioTeacherText: If you want to wake up with great energy, you should turn off your phone screen thirty minutes before sleeping and you shouldn't drink coffee after 5:00 PM.
listening.question: What does the doctor advise teenagers to do before sleeping?

Play video games until 3:00 AM every single night.
Drink three energy drinks before going to bed.
listening.correctAnswerText: Turn off phone screens 30 minutes before sleep and avoid late caffeine.

classes.classTitle: Class 3: Conditions & Scientific Facts (Zero Conditional) / Hechos Científicos y Reglas
classes.classObjective: Explicar leyes científicas, causas y efectos inmediatos, y mecánicas de videojuegos usando el Condicional Cero con precisión.
goals: Dominar la estructura del Zero Conditional: 'If [Present Simple], [Present Simple]'.
Describir hechos científicos, leyes de la naturaleza y reacciones causa-efecto 100% seguras.
Formular preguntas condicionales ('What happens if...?') y responder con fluidez.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Science Fair Experiment / El Experimento de la Feria

sampleDialogue.speaker: Mateo
sampleDialogue.text: Look Valeria! If you mix baking soda and vinegar, it produces carbon dioxide gas instantly!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Mira Valeria! ¡Si mezclas bicarbonato y vinagre, produce gas dióxido de carbono al instante!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valeria
sampleDialogue.text: That is awesome! And what happens when you add red food coloring and liquid soap?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Eso es genial! ¿Y qué pasa cuando le agregas colorante rojo y jabón líquido?

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Physics Professor's Law / La Ley de la Física
listening.transcription: In physics and chemistry, if the temperature of liquid water drops below zero degrees Celsius, it freezes and transforms into solid ice.
listening.audioTeacherText: In physics and chemistry, if the temperature of liquid water drops below zero degrees Celsius, it freezes and transforms into solid ice.
listening.question: What happens when liquid water drops below zero degrees Celsius?
options: It freezes and transforms into solid ice.
It explodes into fire and smoke.
It turns into sweet chocolate milk.
listening.correctAnswerText: It freezes and transforms into solid ice.

classes.classTitle: Class 4: Messaging, Texting & Online Communication / Mensajería y Texting
classes.classObjective: Comunicarse con naturalidad en chats, mensajes directos y redes sociales usando abreviaciones populares y tono digital adecuado.
goals: Dominar los acrónimos de chat más usados: BRB, BTW, TBH, IMO, RN, IDK, NGL.
Escribir mensajes cortos, directos y naturales para grupos de Discord y WhatsApp.
Distinguir entre tono informal para amigos y tono respetuoso para comunidades en línea.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Group Chat Strategy / La Estrategia en el Chat Grupal

sampleDialogue.speaker: Samuel
sampleDialogue.text: Yo everyone! WDYT about playing some ranked matches tonight? TBH, our squad needs a win!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Hola a todos! ¿Qué opinan de jugar unas partidas clasificatorias hoy? Para ser sincero, ¡nuestro equipo necesita ganar!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Daniela
sampleDialogue.text: I'm down! BTW, did you guys finish the English presentation slides RN?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Me apunto! Por cierto, ¿terminaron las diapositivas de la presentación de inglés justo ahora?

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Voice Note from a Gamer / Nota de Voz de un Gamer
listening.transcription: Hey guys! I have terrible lag right now. BRB in five minutes, I will restart my wifi router so we can play the tournament without disconnection.
listening.audioTeacherText: Hey guys! I have terrible lag right now. BRB in five minutes, I will restart my wifi router so we can play the tournament without disconnection.
listening.question: Why is the speaker stepping away for five minutes (BRB)?
options: To restart the wifi router and fix bad internet lag.
To go to sleep until tomorrow morning.
To cook a five-course dinner for his family.
listening.correctAnswerText: To restart the wifi router and fix bad internet lag.

classes.classTitle: Class 5: Future Possibilities & Consequences (First Conditional) / Primer Condicional
classes.classObjective: Expresar posibilidades futuras reales, metas y consecuencias usando If + Presente Simple y Will / Won't con fluidez.
goals: Dominar la fórmula del First Conditional: 'If + Present Simple, will + base verb'.
Expresar consecuencias negativas con 'won't' o 'unless' (a menos que).
Formular preguntas sobre el futuro ('What will you do if...?') y responder con seguridad.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Robotics Competition / La Competencia de Robótica

sampleDialogue.speaker: Mariana
sampleDialogue.text: Nicolás, if our team finishes the robot programming by Thursday, we will qualify for the finals!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Nicolás, si nuestro equipo termina la programación del robot para el jueves, clasificaremos a las finales!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Nicolás
sampleDialogue.text: That is huge! And if we win the first place prize, we will travel to the international robotics expo in Tokyo!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Eso es gigante! Y si ganamos el premio del primer lugar, ¡viajaremos a la expo internacional de robótica en Tokio!

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Coach's Motivation Speech / La Charla del Entrenador
listening.transcription: Listen team: If we train with maximum discipline and support each other on the field, we will lift the championship trophy on Saturday!
listening.audioTeacherText: Listen team: If we train with maximum discipline and support each other on the field, we will lift the championship trophy on Saturday!
listening.question: What will happen if the team trains with discipline and supports each other?
options: They will lift the championship trophy on Saturday.
They will give up and cancel the game.
They will eat pizza and forget the tournament.
listening.correctAnswerText: They will lift the championship trophy on Saturday.

classes.classTitle: Class 6: Comparatives & Superlatives (Tech, Movies & Sports) / Comparativos y Superlativos
classes.classObjective: Comparar y clasificar tecnología, videojuegos, películas y deportistas usando adjetivos comparativos (-er / more than) y superlativos (the -est / the most).
goals: Usar comparativos cortos (-er than) y largos (more ... than) para comparar dos cosas.
Usar superlativos (the -est / the most ...) para destacar el número 1 absoluto de un grupo.
Dominar formas irregulares clave: good ➔ better ➔ the best | bad ➔ worse ➔ the worst.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Tech Review Showdown / El Duelo Tecnológico

sampleDialogue.speaker: David
sampleDialogue.text: In my review, Console X is faster and more powerful than Console Y, but it is also much more expensive!
sampleDialogue.es: En mi reseña, la Consola X es más rápida y potente que la Consola Y, ¡pero también es mucho más costosa!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Laura
sampleDialogue.text: That is true, but Console Y has the most innovative wireless controllers and the best exclusive games library.
sampleDialogue.es: Eso es verdad, pero la Consola Y tiene los controles inalámbricos más innovadores y el mejor catálogo de juegos exclusivos.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Tech Guru's Smartphone Verdict / El Veredicto del Experto
listening.transcription: After testing both models for two weeks, the Pro Edition is clearly the most durable smartphone with the longest battery life on the market.
listening.audioTeacherText: After testing both models for two weeks, the Pro Edition is clearly the most durable smartphone with the longest battery life on the market.
listening.question: What is the expert verdict on the Pro Edition smartphone?
options: It is the most durable smartphone with the longest battery life.
It has the worst battery and breaks immediately.
It is the slowest phone ever invented.
listening.correctAnswerText: It is the most durable smartphone with the longest battery life.

classes.classTitle: Class 7: Too & Enough: Problems and Solutions / Too y Enough para Problemas y Soluciones
classes.classObjective: Explicar problemas de exceso y carencia usando 'too + adjetivo' y 'adjetivo + enough / not enough + sustantivo' con soluciones lógicas.
goals: Usar 'too + adjetivo' para expresar exceso o dificultad ('too expensive', 'too complicated').
Usar 'adjetivo + enough' ('fast enough', 'big enough') y 'not enough + sustantivo' ('not enough time').
Plantear quejas y proponer soluciones inmediatas con fluidez.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Gaming Setup Dilemma / El Dilema del Setup

sampleDialogue.speaker: Andrés
sampleDialogue.text: Valentina, my computer is too slow to run the new graphics update and I don't have enough RAM memory!
sampleDialogue.es: Valentina, ¡mi computador está demasiado lento para correr la nueva actualización gráfica y no tengo suficiente memoria RAM!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: Don't worry Andrés! The graphics card is powerful enough; you just need to close background apps and delete junk files.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡No te preocupes Andrés! La tarjeta gráfica es suficientemente potente; solo necesitas cerrar apps en segundo plano y borrar archivos basura.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Tech Support Hotline / Soporte Técnico
listening.transcription: Your tablet cannot download this 4K video file because you do not have enough storage space on your device. Please delete five gigabytes of old photos first.
listening.audioTeacherText: Your tablet cannot download this 4K video file because you do not have enough storage space on your device. Please delete five gigabytes of old photos first.
listening.question: Why can't the tablet download the 4K video file?
options: Because there is not enough storage space on the device.
Because the screen is too small.
Because the tablet is too new.
listening.correctAnswerText: Because there is not enough storage space on the device.

classes.classTitle: Class 8: Giving Advice to Friends (Should, Shouldn't & Ought to) / Consejos entre Amigos
classes.classObjective: Orientar a amigos en situaciones emocionales y dilemas de amistad usando modales de consejo avanzados con empatía y firmeza.
goals: Dominar modales de recomendación interpersonal: 'You ought to', 'You had better not', 'You should'.
Aconsejar con empatía en dilemas de lealtad, disculpas sinceras y reconciliación.
Expresar sugerencias constructivas ('Why don't you have a private chat with them?').

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Group Project Misunderstanding / El Malentendido Grupal

sampleDialogue.speaker: Juliana
sampleDialogue.text: Felipe, you ought to talk to Sebastián because he feels excluded from our science team presentation.
sampleDialogue.es: Felipe, deberías hablar con Sebastián porque se siente excluido de la presentación del equipo de ciencias.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Felipe
sampleDialogue.text: You're right Juliana. I had better send him an apology message right now and assign him the final experiment slide.
sampleDialogue.es: Tienes razón Juliana. Más vale que le envíe un mensaje de disculpa justo ahora y le asigne la diapositiva del experimento final.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: School Counselor's Friendship Advice / El Consejo de la Orientadora
listening.transcription: When you have an argument with a close friend, you ought to listen with empathy first and you had better not discuss your private issues in public group chats.
listening.audioTeacherText: When you have an argument with a close friend, you ought to listen with empathy first and you had better not discuss your private issues in public group chats.
listening.question: What should teenagers do when having an argument with a friend?
options: Listen with empathy and avoid arguing in public group chats.
Post angry memes about them on social media.
Never speak to them ever again in life.
listening.correctAnswerText: Listen with empathy and avoid arguing in public group chats.

classes.classTitle: Class 9: Informal vs Formal Messages, Emails & Digital Tone / Tono Formal e Informal
classes.classObjective: Escribir correos formales estructurados (saludos, solicitudes con 'Could you please', despedidas formales) y compararlos con mensajes informales.
goals: Dominar saludos formales ('Dear Professor [Name]') vs informales ('Hey guys!').
Formular solicitudes corteses con 'I would like to inquire about...' y 'Could you please clarify...?'.
Cerrar correos con despedidas elegantes: 'Best regards', 'Sincerely', 'Thank you for your time'.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Formal Scholarship Inquiry / La Solicitud de Beca

sampleDialogue.speaker: Manuela
sampleDialogue.text: Dear Professor Hawkins, I am writing to inquire about the application deadlines for the summer exchange program.
sampleDialogue.es: Estimado Profesor Hawkins, le escribo para consultar las fechas límite de postulación para el programa de intercambio de verano.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Prof. Hawkins
sampleDialogue.text: Dear Manuela, thank you for your email. Please find attached the official application guide and scholarship details.
sampleDialogue.es: Estimada Manuela, gracias por su correo. Por favor encuentre adjunta la guía oficial de postulación y los detalles de la beca.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: University Admissions Officer / Admisiones Universitarias
listening.transcription: Good morning candidates. Please submit your official high school transcript and your personal recommendation letter before Friday at 5:00 PM.
listening.audioTeacherText: Good morning candidates. Please submit your official high school transcript and your personal recommendation letter before Friday at 5:00 PM.
listening.question: What must candidates submit before Friday at 5:00 PM?
options: Their official high school transcript and recommendation letter.
Their gaming high scores on social media.
A video of their favorite comedy memes.
listening.correctAnswerText: Their official high school transcript and recommendation letter.

classes.classTitle: Class 10: Teen Leadership, Customer Service & Capstone Review / Liderazgo Juvenil y Proyecto Capstone
classes.classObjective: Integrar opiniones, condicionales (Zero y First), comparativos, modales de consejo y correos formales en un proyecto de liderazgo y graduación de Nivel 4.
goals: Integrar opiniones ('In my opinion'), condicionales ('If we practice, we will succeed') y comparativos.
Resolver situaciones complejas de atención al cliente y mediación de proyectos con diplomacia.
Presentar tu discurso oficial de graduación de Nivel 4 con máxima fluidez y convicción.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Young Innovators Summit / La Cumbre de Jóvenes Innovadores

sampleDialogue.speaker: Santiago

sampleDialogue.es: En nuestra opinión, si los jóvenes reciben entrenamiento práctico de inglés y tecnología, ¡crearán soluciones para todo el mundo!

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: Our community project is more sustainable than previous models, and our team resolved every single challenge with teamwork.
sampleDialogue.es: Nuestro proyecto comunitario es más sostenible que los modelos anteriores, y nuestro equipo resolvió cada desafío con trabajo en equipo.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Academy Director's Graduation Address / Discurso del Director
listening.transcription: Congratulations Level 4 graduates! You have proven that if you dedicate effort and passion to English, you will conquer international opportunities and lead with confidence.
listening.audioTeacherText: Congratulations Level 4 graduates! You have proven that if you dedicate effort and passion to English, you will conquer international opportunities and lead with confidence.
listening.question: What does the academy director say about Level 4 graduates?
options: They have proven that effort and passion lead to international opportunities and confidence.
They should stop practicing English immediately.
They failed all their assessments and need to repeat Level 1.
listening.correctAnswerText: They have proven that effort and passion lead to international opportunities and confidence.

levelTitle: Level 5, 6, 7 - Intermediate (Teen Sharks) / Nivel 5, 6, 7 - Intermediate (Adolescente Sharks)

classes.classTitle: Class 1: My Life Experiences (Present Perfect) / Experiencias de Vida y Present Perfect
classes.classObjective: Describir experiencias de vida memorables, formular y responder preguntas con 'Have you ever...?' y usar adverbios temporales (already, yet, just, never).
goals: Preguntar sobre experiencias con 'Have you ever + [Participio Pasado]?' y responder con fluidez.
Usar los 4 marcadores de experiencia: ALREADY (ya), YET (aún/todavía), JUST (acabar de) y NEVER (nunca).
Diferenciar una experiencia de vida en Present Perfect de un hecho con fecha fija en Pasado Simple.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Adventure Camp Bucket List / El Campamento de Aventura

sampleDialogue.speaker: Andrés
sampleDialogue.text: Valentina, have you ever tried white-water rafting in San Gil?
sampleDialogue.es: Valentina, ¿alguna vez has probado rafting en aguas bravas en San Gil?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Valentina
sampleDialogue.text: Yes, I have! I have already done it twice with my cousins, and it was breathtaking!
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Sí, claro! Ya lo he hecho dos veces con mis primos, ¡y fue impresionante!

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teen Explorer Podcast Interview / Entrevista al Explorador
listening.transcription: I have already visited three South American countries, but I have not seen the Amazon rainforest yet.
listening.audioTeacherText: I have already visited three South American countries, but I have not seen the Amazon rainforest yet.
listening.question: What experience has the speaker already completed and what is still pending?
options: Has visited three South American countries, but hasn't seen the Amazon rainforest yet.
Has lived in Antarctica for ten years.
Has never left his house.
listening.correctAnswerText: Has visited three South American countries, but hasn't seen the Amazon rainforest yet.

classes.classTitle: Class 2: Teen Slang & Phrasal Verbs in Daily Conversations / Slang Juvenil y Phrasal Verbs
classes.classObjective: Usar phrasal verbs cotidianos en conversaciones orales, distinguir significado literal de figurado y sonar natural al interactuar con amigos en inglés.
goals: Dominar 6 phrasal verbs sociales esenciales (hang out, chill out, figure out, turn down, catch up, run into).
Diferenciar el significado literal de un verbo ('turn' = girar) de su phrasal verb ('turn down' = rechazar).
Usar expresiones coloquiales en conversaciones juveniles ('What's up?', 'No way!', 'I'm down!').

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Weekend Squad Hangout / El Plan del Fin de Semana

sampleDialogue.speaker: Camilo
sampleDialogue.text: Hey Natalia! Do you want to hang out at the gaming arcade this Friday after school?
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Hola Natalia! ¿Quieres parchar en la sala de juegos este viernes después del colegio?

sampleDialogue.speaker: Natalia
sampleDialogue.text: I would love to, but I had to turn down two plans already because I need to catch up on my biology homework.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Me encantaría, pero ya tuve que rechazar dos planes porque necesito ponerme al día con la tarea de biología!

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Teen Voice Note from Discord / Nota de Voz de Amigo
listening.transcription: Hey guys! I just ran into Felipe at the park and we decided to hang out at my place to chill out and play video games. Are you down?
listening.audioTeacherText: Hey guys! I just ran into Felipe at the park and we decided to hang out at my place to chill out and play video games. Are you down?
listening.question: What did the speaker and Felipe decide to do?
options: Hang out at his place to chill out and play video games.
Cancel all classes forever.
Go to sleep immediately.
listening.correctAnswerText: Hang out at his place to chill out and play video games.

classes.classTitle: Class 3: Possibilities & Deductions (Must, Might, Can't) / Posibilidades y Deducciones con Modales
classes.classObjective: Expresar grados de certeza lógica usando modales de deducción (must be, might be, can't be) para resolver enigmas y explicar pistas en inglés.
goals: Usar 'Must be' para deducciones 99% seguras basadas en evidencia clara.
Usar 'Might / Could be' para posibilidades intermedias (50%) y 'Can't be' para impossibilidades lógicas (0%).
Resolver misterios juveniles analizando pistas y formulando hipótesis deductivas.

readingContext.title: Reading Studio: The Mystery Locker at High School / El Casillero Misterioso

sampleDialogue.speaker: Daniel
sampleDialogue.text: Look at this unlocked locker! There is a robotics manual and a brand new drone remote inside.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Mira este casillero abierto! Hay un manual de robótica y un control remoto nuevo de dron adentro.

sampleDialogue.speaker: Laura
sampleDialogue.text: It must belong to someone from the STEM club! It can't be Mateo's because he does not do robotics.
sampleDialogue.es: ¡Debe pertenecer a alguien del club de STEM! No puede ser de Mateo porque él no hace robótica.

listening.slideTitle: Listening Lab: Detective Clues Audio Brief / Informe de Pistas
listening.transcription: The chemistry laboratory lights are on and music is playing inside at 8:00 PM. Professor Gomez must still be working on the science fair project.
listening.audioTeacherText: The chemistry laboratory lights are on and music is playing inside at 8:00 PM. Professor Gomez must still be working on the science fair project.
listening.question: What is the logical deduction about Professor Gomez?
options: He must still be working on the science fair project.
He can't be at school because he went to the moon.
The laboratory is completely abandoned.
listening.correctAnswerText: He must still be working on the science fair project.

classes.classTitle: Class 4: If I Ruled the World (Second Conditional) / Segundo Condicional e Hipótesis
classes.classObjective: Expresar hipótesis irreales, debatir qué harías si tuvieras poderes o fueras líder mundial usando 'If I had/were..., I would...' en inglés.
